reading.body:
H.R. 8241 is a one-party energy and data center bill with no recorded lobbying pressure behind it. Its 29 cosponsors are all Democrats, led by sponsor Paul Tonko, and the bill's own text tags it to energy and data centers. The latest status date is 2026-04-09, and no lobbying filing from 2025 or later names it.

The pattern is a bill that has drawn broad but entirely one-sided support. Every cosponsor recorded by LegiScan carries a D, which means the coalition is not bipartisan and the bill's path depends on whether it can move without cross-party votes. The subject tags matter for AI because data centers are the physical layer of compute, and a bill tagged to both energy and data centers sits exactly where power supply and siting decisions get made.

The absence of lobbying filings is the most informative single fact here. A bill that no filing names has not yet become an active target of organized influence, which is consistent with a bill that has not reached a stage where industries need to take positions. That does not mean no one cares, only that no filing in this dataset says so.

What the data does not cover is the bill's actual contents, its committee status, or any vote. It records who sponsored and cosponsored the bill and what issues its text touches, and nothing about what the bill would do or whether it will move.

summary: H.R. 8241, Power for the People Act of 2026. Latest status date 2026-04-09. Issues tagged from the bill's own text: energy and data centers. 0 lobbying filing(s) for 2025 or later name it.
